name: Wei Junjie
bio:
Wei Junjie's path to Formula 1 was unconventional, starting with a degree in organizational psychology rather than motorsport engineering. He discovered his passion for racing during a university internship at a local karting track. Recognizing the importance of human capital in motorsport, he focused his studies on talent management and team dynamics. After graduation, Wei joined a small racing team in Singapore, quickly rising through the ranks due to his keen understanding of employee motivation and his ability to build strong relationships. 

Wei's approach to HR is deeply pragmatic. He believes in data-driven decision-making and prioritizes creating a supportive and efficient work environment where every team member can thrive. He implemented innovative training programs and performance review systems that boosted employee satisfaction and reduced turnover. Wei's reputation for fairness and his ability to navigate complex interpersonal issues has made him a highly respected figure within the paddock. His unique blend of HR expertise and motorsport passion sets him apart, ensuring that Alpine F1's human resources are always performing at their peak.

Moving to Alpine was a big step, but Wei felt it was the right thing to do to expand his skills.

physical.hairStyle: Short, neatly combed with a slight side part
physical.description: Wei is of average height and build, with a friendly and approachable demeanor.

quirks: Always carries a small notebook to jot down observations about team dynamics.
Has a habit of offering practical solutions to problems, even if they're outside his direct responsibility.
Drinks copious amounts of kopi (Singaporean coffee) throughout the day.
